OPENCODE / CONNECTIONS

OpenCode connection errors: fix 401, unavailable models and timeouts

Keep the exact error and identify your OpenCode version and project first. Check credentials for 401/403, the selected model for availability errors, and the service or network for timeouts. Change one thing at a time and retry the same short request before returning to repository work.

Published：2026-11-23 · OpenCode V2

  1. Identify the version and failing project
  2. 401 or 403: check the active account
  3. Model unavailable: check the complete selector
  4. Timeout or uncertain cause: separate service from network
  5. Confirm recovery or prepare a useful report

What happens when the request fails?

Identify the version and failing project

Run opencode --version and record the project directory, selected provider/model and exact error. Service commands and configuration examples here target OpenCode V2. For the older ProviderModelNotFoundError, start with the model checks. Keep a copy of working configuration before upgrading; do not reuse V2-only configuration with V1.

Try a disposable project without private files. Distinguish a startup failure from a model-request failure or a problem isolated to one project. Keep that reproduction fixed while checking each layer.

401 or 403: check the active account

  1. Open /connect in the failing project and confirm the provider and active account. Use its supported sign-in method to replace credentials; keep keys out of project files.
  2. Select an accessible model in /models. For 403, check organization permissions, model entitlement and provider network policies as well as credentials.
  3. Send a short question without repository content, then inspect the response and provider usage. A saved account alone does not establish a working request.

When using environment variables, inspect the server that runs requests. A saved V2 account can take precedence over an environment connection. Check the connection type with opencode auth list and redact account details before sharing output. Switching to another billable account can change who pays for subsequent requests.

Model unavailable: check the complete selector

Choose a listed entry in the current project’s /models rather than guessing a name from an older tutorial. A custom selector uses the provider ID followed by the key in its models map. The separate modelID can specify the upstream request name.

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "company/coder"
}

This example works only after defining the company provider and coder model. Inspect project-root and .opencode/ configuration for overrides. An existing session selection can also override the default. Recovery means the selected model answers a short request in the same project.

For an empty local inventory, use the Ollama connection checks. For a cloud model, return to that account’s access and model list.

Timeout or uncertain cause: separate service from network

Check the V2 background service and its local API:

opencode service status
opencode api get /api/info

If the local API works, inspect the provider endpoint, status and proxy path. Exclude localhost,127.0.0.1,::1 from proxies and ensure the background service receives the intended settings. For a corporate certificate, configure the trusted certificate chain while keeping TLS verification enabled.

After ending the current task, restart a stuck service with opencode service restart; this interrupts active requests. Inspect the matching timestamp in ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log if it still fails. The API check may start the service; it does not verify the external provider.

Confirm recovery or prepare a useful report

Repeat the same short request in the original project and model. Record the response, time and account usage, then resume repository work. Text generation, tool execution and a correctly tested code change are separate checks.

For a report, include the version, OS, timestamp, model ID, redacted configuration and minimal reproduction. Remove keys, authorization headers and private code. Avoid deleting the entire data directory as a first repair: sessions and local state can be lost.
